PullRequest.Title: Keep quick input open while its context menu has focus
PullRequest.Body:

🤖 Closes #153267

### Problem
With HTML (custom) context menus, right-clicking the Command Palette or any quick pick dismisses it as soon as the menu appears. Custom menus are always used on web and by default on desktop with the custom title bar.

The menu takes DOM focus into a context view outside `.quick-input-widget`, and the quick input's focus tracker treats that as a blur and hides. #155546 only changed the z-index. Native macOS menus never move DOM focus, so they were not affected.

### Change: the creator of each menu renders it inside its owner
This follows the existing pattern, where whoever creates a context view passes its parent explicitly (`renderDropdownAsChildElement` / `menuAsChild` → `domForShadowRoot`). No context-menu infrastructure changes and no new API.

- **Quick input toolbars** (title left/right, inline): `renderDropdownAsChildElement: true`, so their overflow menus render inside the quick input.
- **Quick input text input**: when the Clipboard API is available, the quick input opens the context menu of its own input with `domForShadowRoot` set to its widget. Otherwise (e.g. on non-secure origins) it leaves the event to the browser's menu, whose Paste works there. This mirrors the terminal find widget, which already opens `createTextInputActions` for its input itself. It stops the event, so the workbench's generic `TextInputActionsProvider` skips it and exactly one menu opens.
- **Icon picker** (terminal "Change Icon", Agents-window appearance picker): opens the context menu of its search box with `domForShadowRoot` set to its icon grid. The grid owns focus within the picker and refocuses the list when focus leaves it, so the menu has to live inside the grid.
- **`createTextInputActions` moved** from `workbench/browser/actions/textInputActions.ts` to `platform/clipboard/browser/textInputActions.ts` so the platform quick input can use it. Its dependencies were already base/platform only.
  - Paste now keeps the value and selection when `IClipboardService.readText()` returns nothing. The browser clipboard service returns `''` when reading fails, which previously replaced the selection with nothing.
  - As a result, standalone (Monaco) quick input now shows the same custom text input menu as the workbench instead of the browser menu.
- **Quick input owner behaviour for hosted menus:**
  - finish the open motion before a menu is laid out (the motion no longer leaves a transform or `will-change` that would clip the fixed-position menu under Modern UI);
  - close a hosted menu when hiding;
  - dismiss on an outside click, meaning a mouse down on the menu's mouse blocker outside the quick input;
  - keep the menu's keyboard input away from the quick input and its keybindings;
  - clear `inQuickInput` while the menu has focus.

**Not covered: item-row overflow menus.** No quick input item button sets `secondary`, so these menus are not produced today. They are left unchanged: rendered inside a row, the menu would be clipped by the list's transformed rows container. A probe found 0 of 6 items clickable.

Earlier iterations that were rejected:
- deferring the blur while focus is in a context view (couples quick input to context-view focus timing);
- a quick-input-specific `textInputContextMenuActions` option;
- implicit DOM discovery of a "context menu host" in `ContextMenuHandler`, which goes against the creator-owned pattern.

### Tests
- `src/vs/platform/quickinput/test/electron-browser/quickInputFocusOut.test.ts` uses real document focus (via the test runner IPC) and the real `ContextViewService`/`ContextMenuService`/`Menu`, with a generic opener that mirrors `TextInputActionsProvider`. It covers:
  - exactly one `showContextMenu` call, hosted in the widget;
  - Escape keeps focus and selection; Paste success; Paste with an unreadable clipboard keeps value and selection;
  - title/inline toolbar overflow menus;
  - arrow-key and quick-navigation isolation; `inQuickInput`;
  - outside clicks, the menu itself, and overflowing submenu items;
  - focus loss and window blur; hide while open; unrelated menus; `ignoreFocusOut`;
  - an ordinary input outside the quick input is not hosted; row overflow is not hosted;
  - icon picker nested host;
  - motion during and after the open animation.
- `src/vs/workbench/services/userDataProfile/test/browser/iconPicker.test.ts`: the search box menu is opened once with the grid as host, the text input actions, and the input as context.
- `src/vs/platform/clipboard/test/browser/textInputActions.test.ts`: Paste replaces the selection; an empty or unreadable clipboard keeps value and selection.
- Each mutation makes tests fail:
  - removing the quick input `domForShadowRoot`: 13 fail;
  - turning off the toolbars' `renderDropdownAsChildElement`: 4 fail;
  - removing the icon picker's `domForShadowRoot`: 1 fails;
  - removing the Paste guard: 2 fail.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run` on the above plus `contextMenuHandler.test.ts`, all quick input tests and `frostedGlass.test.ts`: 161 passing.
- `npm run eslint`, `npm run typecheck-client`, `npm run monaco-compile-check`, `npm run valid-layers-check`: clean.

### Manual verification
Verified with real pointer input on head 5cfb5101443; the only later change is the Clipboard API check below.

- **Web (code-web, Chromium)**
  - Right-click in the Command Palette keeps the palette open and shows exactly one menu inside it. The menu is unclipped and its bottom item is clickable, also while the open animation is running.
  - Escape keeps focus and selection, and Paste works (stubbed clipboard).
  - When the clipboard cannot be read, Paste keeps the value and selection.
  - Escape on the palette returns focus. One outside click dismisses the menu and the palette.
- **macOS desktop, custom menus**: the same palette behaviour, with Select All instead of Paste.
- **macOS desktop, real Terminal: Change Icon picker**: the search box menu is rendered in the icon grid and the picker stays open. Escape returns to the search box, and Select All works.
- **macOS desktop, native menus**: the palette stays open.
- **Ordinary workbench input (Search view)**: the menu is unchanged and not hosted.
- **Standalone Monaco**: tested with the `test/monaco` harness built from this branch.
  - The quick input shows the custom menu inside itself.
  - With the real Chromium clipboard: Copy puts exactly the selected text on the clipboard, Paste with permission granted inserts the text, Paste with permission denied (`NotAllowedError`) keeps the value and selection, and Select All works. An outside click dismisses.
  - On a non-secure origin without the Clipboard API, the quick input leaves the right-click to the browser's own menu, as on main (checked on 8aa28cc861a).
- **Not reached in the real UI**: toolbar overflow and submenus, because nothing in the product or the extension API produces them. They are covered by the real-focus electron-browser tests.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open and interact with the Command Palette or another quick input, including opening its text-input context menu
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Showing the picker creates/reuses the quick-input UI and starts a 250 ms CSS transform/opacity animation. A pointer/context-menu gesture synchronously queries and finishes only animations on the single widget before the hosted menu is laid out; no subprocess, filesystem, database, network, or IPC work is on the open/menu-render critical path. Clipboard work starts only if Paste is explicitly selected.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read clipboard text through the native host when the user explicitly selects Paste on desktop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one IPC call per explicit Paste action; independent of quick-pick item count and not performed when opening the picker or menu.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The pre-diff workbench TextInputActionsProvider used the same createTextInputActions logic and issued one clipboard read for Paste; the helper was moved without increasing read count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks only completion of the explicit Paste action, not picker opening or context-menu rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the browser Clipboard API to read text on web/standalone.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one browser API call per explicit Paste action; no per-item scaling or retries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Standalone quick input previously relied on the browser's native menu; the application now invokes navigator.clipboard.readText for its custom Paste action. Workbench web quick input already reached the same clipboard service through the generic text-input menu. The changed call remains one user-triggered operation, so it does not establish a performance regression.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks only the selected Paste action. It is off the picker-open and menu-open critical paths.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost is constant per gesture: one widget animation query and an eight-entry menu. Quick-pick item count does not multiply this work because the menu belongs to the input, not each row.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One lazily-created QuickInputController per quick-input service (or per standalone editor scope), one active quick input, and the shared context-view service permits one active context view. There is no fan-out or task burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates in opening or rendering the hosted menu. The controller and UI are lazily created and reused; action arrays are small and bounded. Clipboard reads are intentionally uncached to preserve current clipboard contents.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the call path and constant cardinality from the changed listeners, controller ownership, and context-menu implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser style/animation-query cost and compositor promotion vary by engine, but the query targets one element and is gesture-bound. No evidence shows measurable jank from removing will-change; transform animations are otherwise unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new synchronous DOM work is bounded to one element per user gesture, hosted-menu lifecycle is explicitly closed on hide, and clipboard access remains one explicit action rather than fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a quick-input title/inline toolbar overflow menu
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The toolbar passes its own element as domForShadowRoot, after the container capture listener finishes the opening animation. ContextMenuHandler renders one local Menu and one blocker in the shared context view; there are no external boundaries.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Menu rendering scales with the bounded number of overflow actions in that toolbar, not with quick-pick row count. Current product paths do not produce these overflow menus, further limiting prevalence.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single context view is active globally, so toolbar menu opens are serialized by replacement rather than concurrent.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Toolbar actions already exist on the toolbar; rendering the dropdown does not add a cache or miss path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from ToolBar -> DropdownMenuActionViewItem -> ContextMenuHandler tracing.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact menu DOM cost depends on action count, but no changed code increases that count or repeats rendering.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression. The diff changes the DOM host, not menu cardinality, external calls, or concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Terminal Change Icon or session-group appearance icon picker and use the search-input context menu
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The picker already constructs and lays out its icon grid on invocation. The change adds one delegated contextmenu listener; on right-click it creates eight lightweight actions and renders one hosted menu. Clipboard access occurs only after selecting Paste.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read desktop clipboard text through native-host IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per explicit Paste action, not per icon. The icon registry/grid size does not multiply it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff, the event bubbled to the workbench's generic TextInputActionsProvider, whose Paste action performed the same single clipboard read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only the explicit Paste action waits for the read; picker construction, filtering, and menu opening do not.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read text with navigator.clipboard.readText on web.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per explicit Paste action, independent of icon count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The generic workbench text-input context menu already exposed the same browser clipboard read before this listener hosted the menu locally.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Added work is constant per right-click and does not scale with the number of registered icons. Listener lifetime is bounded by the picker's DisposableStore.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One picker-local listener and disposable store per invocation; the picker is disposed when the operation resolves. The shared context view limits active menus to one.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache. Icon enumeration and grid creation are pre-existing eager work; the added action list is created only on context-menu opening and is fixed-size.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from both terminal/session callers and picker disposal flow.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The existing icon-grid construction can scale with registry size, but the diff neither introduces nor increases that work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff changes menu ownership while preserving one clipboard boundary call and adds no icon-count-scaled work or retention.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use text-input actions in ordinary workbench inputs or Terminal Find after helper relocation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Ordinary inputs retain a lazy, shared eight-action array; Terminal Find still creates the same fixed-size array on a user context-menu gesture. Paste performs one clipboard read.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read clipboard text for Paste through native-host IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per explicit Paste, unchanged by moving the helper.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same implementation and call count existed in the workbench helper before it moved to platform clipboard.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only Paste waits for the call.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read clipboard text with the browser API.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per explicit Paste, unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The moved helper already called IClipboardService.readText once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only Paste waits for the call.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant eight-action allocation where actions are created; no dependence on input length except the existing string splice during Paste.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One context menu and one selected action at a time; no batching or parallel reads.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Workbench generic input actions remain Lazy and shared. Terminal Find remains gesture-created and fixed-size. Clipboard contents are not cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from direct before/after helper comparison and all repository call sites.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large pasted strings still allocate proportional to input plus clipboard length, but that mechanism is pre-existing and not materially amplified.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression. The relocation preserves allocation and boundary cardinality; the empty-read guard can only avoid an unnecessary string rewrite and input event.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 10 changed files and traced quick-input, toolbar, icon-picker, context-view, animation, and clipboard paths. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression was found; changed work is gesture-bound and constant-cardinality, external clipboard reads remain one per explicit Paste, and menu/listener lifecycle is bounded and disposed.
